title: Annihilator duality for finite abelian character groups
statement: Let $E$ be a finite abelian group, written multiplicatively, and let $T$ be a commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], with $T^\times$ its group of invertible elements. Put $e=\exp(E)$, the least positive integer such that $g^e=1$ for every $g\in E$. Assume that the group $\mu_e(T)=\{z\in T^\times:z^e=1\}$ is cyclic and contains an element of order exactly $e$. Write $E^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}(E,T^\times)$, with pointwise multiplication. For $K\le E$ put $K^\perp=\{\lambda\in E^\vee:\lambda(k)=1\text{ for every }k\in K\}$. This is an order reversing bijection between subgroups of $E$ and subgroups of $E^\vee$. Its inverse sends a subgroup $D\le E^\vee$ to $D^\perp=\{g\in E:\lambda(g)=1\text{ for every }\lambda\in D\}$. In particular $(D^\perp)^\perp=D$.

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7: equivariant modification X double-prime and log-smooth quotient X double-prime/H. Supporting construction and local calculations in ILO VIII 4--5 and X 1.2--1.8. Supporting input: Exposé VI Proposition 3.5(b), printed p.74, and proof 3.7(b), diagram (3.b), map (3.c), and Nakayama argument, printed pp.75–76. The cyclotomic coefficient base can be absorbed into the strict chart maps to the integral monoid rings.
